    *   Claim 3: C < A (C comes before A)

        1.  (A, B, C):
            *   A < B (True)
            *   B < C (True)
            *   C < A (False, A is before C)

            *   A < B (True)
            *   B < C (False, C is before B)
            *   C < A (False)
        3.  (B, A, C):

            *   B < C (True)
            *   C < A (False)

            *   B < C (True)
            *   C < A (True)

            *   C < A (True)

            *   A < B (False)
            *   B < C (False)
            *   C < A (True)

    *   None of the permutations satisfy all three claims.

    *   In a strict ordering (a total order), there can be no cycles.
